original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Prove that a closed length-28 word over eight letters with multiplicities (4,4,4,4,4,4,2,2) has at most 23 distinct unordered adjacent pairs, that 23 is attained, and that at least five weight-2 basis sums therefore require arcs of length at least four.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one new connector operation. This package keeps the singleton alphabet and adds a necessary condition on the closed word that acts as the connector interface. It answers no part of the card's budget question and does not change kappa.
bottleneck_link: A universal length-28 singleton word would make the #5234 floor of 28 sharp and could lower the eight-source query bill. The bound restricts any future census to words with at most 23 distinct adjacent pairs and excludes the all-distinct Euler-circuit route.
stop_rule: Stop once the degree count, the complement bound, the sharp example and the exhaustive lemma check are complete. Do not search for a universal word and do not treat an unfinished search as nonexistence.
evidence: Written degree count on the adjacent-pair graph plus an explicit loop-free Eulerian multigraph with degree sequence (8,8,8,8,8,8,4,4) and 23 distinct edges. The verifier exhaustively checks the incidence identity and degree bound on 484,417 closed words over at most five letters, the complement arithmetic, the Euler circuit and the sharp word, and the all-distinct arithmetic.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does a universal length-28 word with multiplicities (4,4,4,4,4,4,2,2) exist?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A yes answer makes the #5234 floor of 28 sharp; a no answer raises f(8) to at least 29.
open_questions.first_step: Restrict a census to words with at most 23 distinct adjacent pairs and at least five repeated slots, then combine with the arc-rank rank-at-least-4 case left open by #6966.
open_questions.blocked_by: No structural exclusion of the remaining adjacency profiles, and no completed census.

open_questions.question: Can length-3 and length-4 arc constraints sharpen the 23-pair bound?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The present count uses only two-letter arcs, and the sharp example shows the two-letter budget alone cannot exclude the profile.
open_questions.first_step: Repeat the degree count on the graph whose edges are distinct length-4 arcs, with the loop and multiplicity bookkeeping of Lemma 1.
open_questions.blocked_by: Length-4 arcs are not determined by adjacent pairs, so the incidence identity needs a new carrier.

open_questions.question: Do the 23-pair bound and the #6966 arc-rank constraint jointly exclude the rank-4 arcs?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That is the only case #6966 leaves open in the rank-at-most-4 part of the length-28 question.
open_questions.first_step: Fix a multiplicity-2 source, enumerate the possible adjacent-pair graphs with at most 23 edges, and test the four-value flat-coordinate count of #6966.
open_questions.blocked_by: No classification of the admissible adjacent-pair graphs up to relabelling.

claim_type: scoped written proof with exhaustive finite corroboration and an explicit sharp example
unrun_obligations: No construction or exclusion of a universal length-28 word.
No replay of the cited #5234 floor or the #3058 f(7)=24 theorem.
No selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, supplier admission or kappa change.
No proof-kernel or independent human review.
